title: Cooper Sharp Chopped Ribeye Hoagies
seoTitle: Cooper Sharp Chopped Ribeye Hoagies | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Philly on the flat-top—chopped ribeye, whiz optional, ten hoagies fast
subtitle: Chopped ribeye, griddled onions, and melted provolone for ten
description: Ribeye slices freeze partially and chop fine, griddle with onions until charred, melt provolone, and pile on toasted hoagie rolls for ten cheesesteaks.

steps.title: Prep ribeye for chopping
steps.instruction: Partially freeze ribeye 45 minutes. Slice thin, then chop fine with bench scraper.

steps.title: Slice onions
steps.instruction: Slice onions paper-thin for quick caramelization on the griddle.

steps.title: Heat flat-top
steps.instruction: Preheat griddle to 425°F. Film with oil.

steps.title: Griddle onions
steps.instruction: Griddle onions 8–10 minutes until soft and golden. Push to cooler zone.

steps.title: Chop and sear beef
steps.instruction: Griddle chopped ribeye in batches, chopping with spatulas on the flat-top until charred and 145°F.

steps.title: Melt cheese
steps.instruction: Combine beef with onions, lay provolone over top, cover with dome or foil until melted.

steps.title: Toast rolls
steps.instruction: Split hoagies and toast cut-side down on griddle at 375°F until crisp.

steps.title: Line for ten
steps.instruction: Pile cheesesteak mix into rolls. About 8 oz beef per sandwich. Hot peppers on request.

proTips: Partially frozen ribeye chops cleaner—warm steak shreds on the flat-top.
Chop meat on the griddle with two spatulas for authentic texture.
Provolone under a dome melts evenly without drying beef.
tonightSpread: Flat-top Philly cheesesteaks with hot cherry peppers.
French fries or onion rings on the side.
leftovers: Chopped beef into breakfast hoagie with eggs.
Cheesesteak egg rolls if feeling ambitious.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Cheesesteaks are flat-top food—fast, loud, and filling. Chopped beef holds at 170°F; rolls toast while meat finishes between calls.
mealPrepNotes: Partially freeze ribeye for clean chopping. Griddle at 425°F in batches. Hold chopped beef and onions at 170°F up to 30 minutes. Build steaks to order.
